eras.name: Creation
eras.eraDescription: The primordial age when the cosmos was formed from chaos. Tiamat and Apsu existed before all others.

eras.name: Age of the First Gods
eras.eraDescription: The great gods emerged — Anu took the heavens, Enlil the earth, Enki the waters.

eras.name: Anunnaki on Earth
eras.eraDescription: The Anunnaki descended to Earth, established cities, and began mining operations according to Sumerian texts.

eras.name: Creation of Mankind
eras.eraDescription: Humans were created to relieve the gods of labor. Enki and Ninhursag fashioned mankind from clay.

eras.name: Antediluvian Period
eras.eraDescription: The age of the antediluvian kings with impossibly long reigns, as recorded in the Sumerian King List.

eras.name: The Great Flood
eras.eraDescription: Enlil sent the deluge to destroy mankind. Ziusudra/Utnapishtim survived by building an ark on Enki's warning.

eras.name: Post-Flood Kingdoms
eras.eraDescription: Kingship descended from heaven again. The dynasties of Kish, Uruk, and Ur arose.

eras.name: Early Dynastic Period
eras.eraDescription: Historical kings emerge alongside legendary ones. Gilgamesh rules Uruk. The gods still intervene directly.

eras.name: Antediluvian
eras.eraDescription: The mythical kings who ruled before the Great Flood, with reigns lasting tens of thousands of years.

eras.name: First dynasty of Kish
eras.eraDescription: The first dynasty to receive kingship after the Flood according to the Sumerian King List.

eras.name: First rulers of Uruk
eras.eraDescription: The early rulers of Uruk, including the legendary Mesh-ki-ang-gasher, Enmerkar, and Lugalbanda.

eras.name: First dynasty of Ur
eras.eraDescription: The first dynasty of the city of Ur, including Mesh-Ane-pada.

eras.name: Dynasty of Awan
eras.eraDescription: An Elamite dynasty from the region of Awan that briefly held kingship.

eras.name: Second dynasty of Kish
eras.eraDescription: The second dynasty of Kish, including rulers with epithets like 'the fuller' and 'the boatman'.

eras.name: Dynasty of Hamazi
eras.eraDescription: A dynasty from the city of Hamazi in the Zagros region.

eras.name: Second dynasty of Uruk
eras.eraDescription: The second dynasty of Uruk, including En-shag-kush-ana.

eras.name: Second dynasty of Ur
eras.eraDescription: The second dynasty of Ur, including Nanni and his son Mesh-ki-ang-Nanna.

eras.name: Dynasty of Adab
eras.eraDescription: The dynasty of the city of Adab, including Lugal-Ane-mundu.

eras.name: Dynasty of Mari
eras.eraDescription: The dynasty of the city of Mari, including Anbu, Anba, Bazi, and others.

eras.name: Third dynasty of Kish
eras.eraDescription: The third dynasty of Kish, including the only woman on the King List: Kug-Bau.

eras.name: Dynasty of Akshak
eras.eraDescription: The dynasty of the city of Akshak, including Puzur-Nirah and Shu-Suen.

eras.name: Fourth dynasty of Kish
eras.eraDescription: The fourth dynasty of Kish, including Puzur-Suen and Ur-Zababa. Sargon was Ur-Zababa's cup-bearer.

eras.name: Third dynasty of Uruk
eras.eraDescription: The third dynasty of Uruk, including Lugal-zage-si who ruled all of Sumer.

eras.name: Dynasty of Akkad
eras.eraDescription: The Akkadian Empire founded by Sargon, the first empire in history.

eras.name: Fourth dynasty of Uruk
eras.eraDescription: The fourth dynasty of Uruk, including Ur-nigin, Ur-gigir, and Ur-Utu.

eras.name: Gutian rule
eras.eraDescription: The rule of Gutian kings from the Zagros mountains over Mesopotamia.

eras.name: Fifth dynasty of Uruk
eras.eraDescription: The fifth dynasty of Uruk, including Utu-hengal who drove out the Gutians.

eras.name: Third dynasty of Ur
eras.eraDescription: The Neo-Sumerian Ur III empire, including Ur-Namma, Shulgi, and Shu-Suen.

eras.name: Dynasty of Isin
eras.eraDescription: The Isin dynasty that ruled after the fall of Ur, including Ishbi-Erra and Lipit-Eshtar.

figures.name: Tiamat
figures.title: Primordial Mother of the Gods
figures.figureDescription: The primordial goddess of the salt sea. Her body was split by Marduk to form heaven and earth.

figures.name: Apsu
figures.title: Primordial Father
figures.figureDescription: The primordial god of fresh water beneath the earth. Slain by Enki/Ea who built his temple upon him.

figures.name: Anshar
figures.title: Whole Sky
figures.figureDescription: Primordial god representing the whole sky. Father of Anu.

figures.name: Kishar
figures.title: Whole Earth
figures.figureDescription: Primordial goddess representing the whole earth. Mother of Anu.

figures.name: Anu
figures.title: King of the Gods, Father of the Heavens
figures.figureDescription: Supreme god of the Sumerian/Akkadian pantheon. Ruled from the heavens. Father of Enlil, Enki, and many others.

figures.name: Antu
figures.title: Queen of the Heavens
figures.figureDescription: Consort of Anu and mother goddess of the heavens.

figures.name: Enlil
figures.title: Lord of the Wind, King of the Earth
figures.figureDescription: Chief deity of the Sumerian pantheon after Anu. Commander of the Anunnaki on Earth. Decreed the Flood.

figures.name: Ninlil
figures.title: Lady of the Wind
figures.figureDescription: Consort of Enlil. Mother of Nanna/Sin the moon god.

figures.name: Enki
figures.title: Lord of the Earth, God of Wisdom
figures.figureDescription: God of wisdom, fresh water, and creation. Warned Ziusudra of the Flood. Co-created humans with Ninhursag.

figures.name: Ninhursag
figures.title: Lady of the Mountain
figures.figureDescription: Mother goddess. Worked with Enki to create mankind from clay mixed with divine blood.

figures.name: Nanna/Sin
figures.title: Lord of the Moon
figures.figureDescription: Moon god, son of Enlil and Ninlil. Father of Utu/Shamash and Inanna/Ishtar. Chief deity of Ur.

figures.name: Ningal
figures.title: Great Lady
figures.figureDescription: Consort of Nanna/Sin. Mother of Utu and Inanna.

figures.name: Utu/Shamash
figures.title: Sun God, Lord of Justice
figures.figureDescription: Sun god and divine judge. Aided Gilgamesh in his quest against Humbaba.

figures.name: Inanna/Ishtar
figures.title: Queen of Heaven
figures.figureDescription: Goddess of love, beauty, sex, war, and political power. Descended to the underworld and returned.

figures.name: Marduk
figures.title: King of the Gods (Babylon)
figures.figureDescription: Chief deity of Babylon. Slew Tiamat and created the world from her body. Son of Enki/Ea.

figures.name: Nabu
figures.title: God of Scribes
figures.figureDescription: God of writing and wisdom. Son of Marduk. Patron of scribes and scholars.

figures.name: Ereshkigal
figures.title: Queen of the Underworld
figures.figureDescription: Ruler of the underworld (Kur/Irkalla). Sister of Inanna. Held power over the dead.

figures.name: Nergal
figures.title: Lord of the Underworld
figures.figureDescription: God of war and plague who became co-ruler of the underworld with Ereshkigal.

figures.name: Ninurta
figures.title: Lord of the Plow
figures.figureDescription: Warrior god and god of agriculture. Son of Enlil. Defeated the Anzu bird.

figures.name: Dumuzi/Tammuz
figures.title: The Shepherd King
figures.figureDescription: Shepherd god and consort of Inanna. Sent to the underworld as her substitute.

figures.name: Adapa
figures.title: First Sage
figures.figureDescription: First of the Seven Sages (Apkallu). Created by Enki as a model human. Refused the food of immortality.

figures.name: Ziusudra/Utnapishtim
figures.title: He Who Found Long Life
figures.figureDescription: Survivor of the Great Flood. Warned by Enki, he built an ark. Granted immortality by the gods afterward.

figures.name: Gilgamesh
figures.title: King of Uruk
figures.figureDescription: Two-thirds divine, one-third human. King of Uruk who sought eternal life after the death of Enkidu.

figures.name: Lugalbanda
figures.title: King of Uruk
figures.figureDescription: Legendary king of Uruk. Father of Gilgamesh. Deified after death.

figures.name: Ninsun
figures.title: Lady Wild Cow
figures.figureDescription: Goddess and mother of Gilgamesh. Known for her wisdom and ability to interpret dreams.

figures.name: Enkidu
figures.title: Wild Man, Friend of Gilgamesh
figures.figureDescription: Created by the gods from clay as a companion and equal to Gilgamesh. Raised among animals.

figures.name: Etana
figures.title: King of Kish
figures.figureDescription: First king after the Flood according to the Sumerian King List. Ascended to heaven on an eagle.

figures.name: Sarpanit
figures.title: Lady of Babylon, Shining One
figures.figureDescription: Consort of Marduk and chief goddess of Babylon. Mother of Nabu. Central figure in the Akitu New Year festival. Worshipped in the Esagila temple.

events.name: Slaying of Apsu
events.eventDescription: Enki/Ea put Apsu into a deep sleep and slew him, then built his temple upon the body.

events.name: Slaying of Tiamat
events.eventDescription: Marduk defeated Tiamat in single combat, split her body to form heaven and earth.

events.name: Creation of Mankind
events.eventDescription: Enki and Ninhursag created humans from clay mixed with the blood of the slain god Kingu.

events.name: Inanna's Descent to the Underworld
events.eventDescription: Inanna descended through the seven gates of the underworld to confront her sister Ereshkigal.

events.name: The Great Flood
events.eventDescription: Enlil decreed the destruction of mankind by flood. Enki warned Ziusudra who built an ark and survived.

events.name: Gilgamesh and Enkidu Slay Humbaba
events.eventDescription: Gilgamesh and Enkidu journeyed to the Cedar Forest and slew its guardian Humbaba.

events.name: Death of Enkidu
events.eventDescription: The gods decreed Enkidu's death as punishment for slaying Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven.

events.name: Gilgamesh Seeks Immortality
events.eventDescription: After Enkidu's death, Gilgamesh journeyed to find Utnapishtim and the secret of eternal life.

events.name: Etana's Ascent to Heaven
events.eventDescription: King Etana rode an eagle to heaven seeking the plant of birth to produce an heir.

events.name: Founding of Eridu
events.eventDescription: The first city was established by the gods. Kingship first descended from heaven here.

sources.name: Enuma Elish
sources.author: Unknown (Babylonian priests)
sources.period: Old Babylonian (~1900-1600 BCE), copies from Neo-Assyrian period
sources.sourceDescription: The Babylonian creation epic. Seven tablets describing Marduk's rise to supremacy, the slaying of Tiamat, and the creation of the world and mankind.
sources.publicationInfo: Multiple tablets, primarily from Ashurbanipal's library at Nineveh (British Museum)

sources.name: Atra-Hasis
sources.author: Ku-Aya (scribe, Old Babylonian period)
sources.sourceDescription: Epic of creation, the burden of the gods, the creation of mankind, and the Great Flood. Key source for understanding why humans were created.
sources.publicationInfo: British Museum tablets, primary copy BM 78941

sources.name: Epic of Gilgamesh
sources.author: Sin-leqi-unninni (Standard Babylonian version)
sources.period: Old Babylonian origins (~2100 BCE), Standard version (~1200 BCE)
sources.sourceDescription: The oldest great work of literature. Twelve tablets following King Gilgamesh of Uruk in his quest for immortality after the death of his friend Enkidu.
sources.publicationInfo: Ashurbanipal's library, Nineveh. Multiple fragments from across Mesopotamia.

sources.name: Inanna's Descent to the Underworld
sources.author: Unknown
sources.sourceDescription: Myth of Inanna's journey through the seven gates of the underworld to confront her sister Ereshkigal, her death and resurrection.

sources.name: Enlil and Ninlil
sources.author: Unknown
sources.sourceDescription: Myth describing the courtship of Enlil and Ninlil and the conception of the moon god Nanna/Sin.

sources.name: Sumerian King List
sources.author: Unknown (multiple scribes)
sources.period: Ur III period (~2100 BCE), copies through Isin-Larsa period
sources.sourceDescription: Records the succession of kings from the time 'kingship descended from heaven' through the antediluvian period, the Flood, and into historical dynasties.

sources.name: Adapa Myth
sources.author: Unknown
sources.period: Middle Babylonian (~14th century BCE, Amarna tablets)
sources.sourceDescription: Story of Adapa, the first sage created by Enki, who was offered but refused the food of immortality when brought before Anu.
sources.publicationInfo: Amarna tablets (EA 356) and Ashurbanipal's library fragments

sources.name: Nergal and Ereshkigal
sources.author: Unknown
sources.period: Middle Babylonian (~14th century BCE), later copies
sources.sourceDescription: Myth explaining how Nergal descended to the underworld and became co-ruler with Ereshkigal through a combination of force and love.

sources.name: Lugal-e
sources.author: Unknown
sources.sourceDescription: Epic of Ninurta's victory over the demon Asag and his ordering of the world. Full title: 'O King, the storm whose splendour is lordly.'

sources.name: Etana Myth
sources.author: Unknown
sources.period: Old Babylonian (~1800 BCE), copies through Neo-Assyrian period
sources.sourceDescription: Story of King Etana of Kish who ascended to heaven on the back of an eagle seeking the plant of birth.
sources.publicationInfo: Multiple fragments, Old Babylonian through Neo-Assyrian

sources.name: Myths from Mesopotamia
sources.author: Stephanie Dalley
sources.sourceDescription: Authoritative English translations of major Mesopotamian myths including Atrahasis, Gilgamesh, Enuma Elish, Etana, Anzu, and Descent of Ishtar.
sources.publicationInfo: Oxford University Press, Oxford World's Classics

sources.name: ETCSL (Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature)
sources.author: University of Oxford
sources.sourceDescription: Comprehensive online corpus of Sumerian literary texts with translations. Major reference for Sumerian myths, hymns, and royal inscriptions.
sources.publicationInfo: Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Oxford
